passage:
A history museum added smell boxes to an exhibit about old city life. Visitors could smell tea leaves, wood smoke, ink, sea air, and machine oil.
Some people laughed at the idea, but many stayed longer at the exhibit. The smells made the past feel closer than pictures alone.
A student said the machine oil helped him imagine factory workers better than the photo did.
The guide explained that history was not lived only through eyes. People heard, smelled, touched, and tasted their worlds.
The smell boxes reminded visitors that learning can enter through many doors. Sometimes the nose opens memory faster than words.
